texts.li: [soldier,winter] A traveler in an old army greatcoat came through the snow asking for {A_nameDef}. It's {X_nameDef}, who shared a tent with {A_objective} through the worst winter of the war. {X_nameDef} has nowhere to spend this one, and asks to stay.

[outlaw,lowtech] {X_nameDef} rode up to the gate on a stolen-looking horse and asked for {A_nameDef} by an old nickname. They ran together on the roads, years ago. {X_nameDef} says {X_pronoun} is honest now, and would like a place here.

[soldier,partner] {X_nameDef}, who served beside {A_nameDef} years ago, has turned up at the gate with a pack and a hopeful look. {A_nameDef}'s partner has heard a great deal about {X_nameDef} over the years, not all of it flattering. {X_nameDef} asks to stay.

lines.li: [soldier] {X_nameDef} and {A_nameDef} stayed up late, drinking to the names of the people who didn't come home. {X_nameDef} lives here now.

texts.li: [winter] A figure came out of the snow at dusk and asked for {A_nameDef}. It's {X_nameDef}, {A_possessive} {RELATION}, who heard a rumor last autumn that {A_nameDef} was alive and has been walking ever since. {X_nameDef} asks to stay.

[farmer] {X_nameDef}, {A_nameDef}'s {RELATION}, has found {A_objective} at last. After the farm was lost, the family scattered, and {X_nameDef} has been asking for {A_nameDef} in every market town since. {X_nameDef} would like to stay.

[lowtech] {X_nameDef} came to the gate with a bundle on {X_possessive} back and asked for {A_nameDef}. They were sweethearts once, in another village, before everything went wrong. {X_nameDef} has no one else to go to, and asks to stay.

[!lowtech,partner] {X_nameDef} has turned up at the colony, asking for {A_nameDef}. They lived together once, before the colony, and parted badly. {A_nameDef}'s partner was in the room when the name was said, and hasn't said a word since.

[quit,winter] {X_nameDef}, who walked out on the colony, has walked back in out of the snow, thin and cold and not proud anymore. {X_nameDef} asks to come home. {A_nameDef} found {X_objective} at the gate and brought the request in.

[banished,winter] {X_nameDef}, who was sent away, has spent the winter somewhere hard and come back to the gate asking for one more chance. {A_nameDef} brought out a blanket before anyone could decide anything.

[trader,!lowtech] A man in a good suit and bad boots has come up the road with a ledger. {A_nameDef} owes his employers {COUNT} silver from a deal that went sour years ago, and the interest, he says, has been very patient.

[outlaw,lowtech] A one-eyed stranger has come to the gate asking for {A_nameDef}, and {A_nameDef} went pale at the sight of the stranger. {A_nameDef} owes {COUNT} silver to the band {A_pronoun} used to ride with, and they've sent someone to collect.
[farmer] Word has come that the old farmer {A_nameDef} worked for as a youngster has died, and left {A_nameDef} a share of what the farm was worth. A cart brought it to the gate this morning.
[artisan] {A_nameDef}'s old master has died and left {A_objective} a chest from the workshop. It came with the next caravan and a short note in the master's hand: "For the one who listened."
[trader] An old trading partner of {A_nameDef}'s has died, and the will names {A_objective}. A courier brought the bequest to the gate, with a list of debts the partner swore were all paid.

[Cooking] A letter has come for {A_nameDef} from the cook who taught {A_objective}, years ago, to make bread. It's mostly a recipe, with corrections, and a line at the bottom saying {A_nameDef} never measured the salt.
[Medicine] {A_nameDef}'s old teacher of medicine has sent a letter, much traveled, asking whether {A_nameDef} still boils {A_possessive} needles. There are three pages of new remedies after that.

[Construction] A note has reached {A_nameDef} from the builder who taught {A_objective} the trade. It says only: "Heard you're building walls now. Mind the corners." {A_nameDef} has read it many times.
[Shooting] {A_nameDef}'s old shooting instructor has sent word, by way of a passing hunter: still alive, still sure {A_nameDef} flinches, and proud anyway.
[scholar] A letter has caught up with {A_nameDef}: the library where {A_pronoun} studied survived the troubles, and someone there still has {A_possessive} old notes on a shelf.
[healer] Word has come that the clinic {A_nameDef} once worked in has reopened, and the people there still speak of {A_objective}.
[artisan] {A_nameDef} heard from a traveler that the workshop {A_pronoun} trained in is busier than ever, and the old master still uses {A_nameDef}'s work to show apprentices how it's done.
[trader] News came with a caravan: the trading house {A_nameDef} worked for has paid off every debt it had, and {A_nameDef}'s name is on the list of people it thanks.
[farmer] A traveler told {A_nameDef} that the farm country {A_pronoun} came from has gone back to scrub. The families left one by one after the bad years, and the last of them went this spring.
[lowtech,winter] News came with the winter's last traveler: the town {A_nameDef} grew up in was emptied by sickness, and nobody lives there now.
